source_text: Nam pergebamus in Numidiam simul, ut semper antea, socio parique comitatu ingressi uiam, quae nos ad exoptatum fidei ac religionis obsequium, illos iam ducebat ad caelum. Et ueneramus ad locum qui appellatur Muguas, cui est Cirtensis coloniae suburbana uicinitas, in qua tunc maxime ciuitate gentilium caeco furore et officiis militaribus persecutionis impetus quasi fluctus saeculi tumescebant, et auidis faucibus ad tentandam iustorum fidem rabies diaboli infestantis inhiabat. Unde Marianus et Iacobus beatissimi martyres certissime exoptata diuinae in se dignationis signa tenuerunt, qui in ea regione, in qua persecutionis tempestas turbulentius fureret, hora iam maturante deducti intellegebant sua Christo gubernante ad ipsum coronae locum directa uestigia. Namque omnes dilectos dei cruenti et caecati praesidis furor per militares manus infensis et infestantibus animis requirebat. Nec in hos solos crudelitatis exercebatur insania, qui superioribus persecutionibus inconcussi libere deo uiuerent, sed in illos quoque manum diabolus insatiabilem porrigebat, quos iamdudum in exilia submotos, etsi nondum sanguine, mente iam martyras, ferox praesidis amentia coronarat.
thought_title: The road into persecution at Cirta
orientation: The narrator, a close friend of Marian and James, tells how they traveled together into Numidia and reached Muguas near Cirta as persecution was swelling.
pass_a_gloss: For we were going into Numidia together, as always before, having entered the road with allied and equal company, which was leading us to the desired service of faith and religion, but was already leading them to heaven. And we had come to the place which is called Muguas, to which belongs the suburban nearness of the colony of Cirta, in which city at that time especially the onsets of persecution were swelling like waves of the world with the blind fury of the pagans and with military services, and with greedy jaws the rage of the attacking devil was gaping open to test the faith of the just. From this Marian and James, most blessed martyrs, most certainly obtained the desired signs of the divine gracious favor in themselves, who, led down in that region in which the storm of persecution was raging more violently, with the hour now ripening, were understanding that their steps, with Christ directing, had been directed to the very place of the crown. For the fury of the bloody and blinded governor was seeking out all those beloved by God through military hands with hostile and attacking minds. And the madness of cruelty was not exercised against these alone, who in earlier persecutions unshaken were living freely for God, but the insatiable devil was also stretching his hand against those also, whom sent away long ago into exiles, although not yet martyrs in blood, already martyrs in mind, the fierce madness of the governor had crowned.

contrasts with sanguine and keeps already called martyrs before death

pass_b_english: We were traveling into Numidia together, as we had always traveled before, companions sharing one road in equal fellowship. That road was leading us toward the longed-for service of faith and devotion, and it was already leading them toward heaven. We had come to a place called Muguas, lying close beside the suburbs of the colony of Cirta. In that city especially the blind rage of the pagans was then swelling like the waves of this world through the action of soldiers, and the raging devil who attacked us was gaping with greedy jaws to test the faith of the righteous.

There the blessed martyrs Marian and James grasped with full certainty the long-desired signs of divine gracious favor at work in themselves. They had been brought into the very district where the storm of persecution raged most fiercely, and with their hour now ripening they understood that Christ was guiding their steps straight to the place of the crown. For the bloody fury of the blinded governor was hunting down all those beloved by God through the hands of soldiers with hostile and aggressive intent. Nor did the madness of cruelty spend itself only on those who had lived freely for God and stood unshaken through earlier persecutions. The insatiable devil was also reaching out his hand against those whom the fierce madness of the governor had removed into exile long ago and had crowned, though not yet in blood, already martyrs in mind.
